scopeDecisions.decision: Conditions observable with unary requests belong to FS-RULES, where they are VERIFIED, and are not conditions here: principals on get, batchGet, runQuery and writes (FS-RULES/principals, query-proofs, document-access), credential refusals of expired, empty, malformed, tampered and unsigned bearers (refusal-shape, token-expiry), unexpired tokens of revoked, disabled and deleted accounts (token-states), claim changes seen only after a refresh (auth-token-fields), and multi-write atomicity after an Auth change (atomic-writes, token-states). A bearer issued by another project's Auth was never recorded there and stays here (foreign-project-token).

Production refuses an end user's read-write transaction (BeginTransaction and newTransaction.readWrite) and allows read-only ones, in two recordings (FS-RULES/document-access); this is a production dependency boundary. Principal binding of the read-only transaction and the Web SDK's optimistic transaction are observed here; generic transaction semantics (snapshots, conflict, retry, expiry, rollback) belong to FS-TRANSACTION.
Applying FS-RULES R2 (owner, 2026-09-24): catalog cases 106 (sign-out) and 109/109C (revocation) move here from FS-LISTEN-SDK; 106N and 108/108C, which involve no Auth state change, stay there.

The oracle is fireemu-oracle-idp/(default), whose Firestore and Rules this lane owns during its runs. Runs are serialized with AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING and AUTH-FEDERATION under the shared lock; each run reads the project's configuration at start and restores and reads back that baseline. Tenants are created and deleted as fixture setup, not as tenant administration semantics (AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING).
State changes during a listen are probed by commits made after the change; a quiet window alone is never evidence that nothing happens.

Token minting and refresh belong to AUTH-CREDENTIAL, the Rules language to FS-RULES, listens without an Auth state change to FS-LISTEN-SDK, tenant administration to AUTH-TENANT-BLOCKING and server-side transaction semantics to FS-TRANSACTION.
As in FS-RULES R9, rows are compared under the strict profile; the emulator profile keeps accepting unsigned emulator tokens and adds no refusal the official emulator does not make.

Production runs in two stages: stage 1 records the unary conditions (tenant-same-uid, read-only-transaction-binding, foreign-project-token); stage 2 records the listener and SDK conditions after fireemu follows stage 1.
An observed difference is decided row by row by the owner, only after two recordings and the final-artifact comparison; no predicted outcome is approved in advance.
Android and Apple SDKs are out of scope; the declared SDK matrix has only the Web SDK.

The sandbox changes on fireemu-oracle-idp (the cloud.firestore release and rulesets, multiTenant.allowTenants, tenants and test accounts per recording, and an IAM binding limited to signJwt) are approved as a policy on FS-RULES R1, R7 and R8 terms: each run restores and reads back the baseline read at its start. Their exact content is approved with each packet.
Each stage-2 recording holds one listen window of about 65 minutes, past the token's expiry (3600 s plus the ~30 s allowance), under the shared lock; the coordinator assigns the time.
The Node Web SDK 12.18.0 and native REST/gRPC are required for the SDK conditions; a real browser is required only for listen-sign-out-and-switch and pending-write-across-switch.

A token of another project is obtained by creating one @example.com test user on fireemu-oracle-query, taking its ID token and deleting the user at once (as approved in the owner ledger on 2026-09-25 for that project).

productionPlan.costBasis: Firestore document reads and writes in the hundreds per recording and a few Identity Platform monthly active users; estimated under US$1 per stage against the US$10 per-task budget. Each packet prices its actual operation mix.
productionPlan.wallTime: Stage 2 holds a listen window of about 65 minutes per recording (OX-3).

conditions.note: The same UID in two tenants of the project is told apart by Rules, and an unexpired ID token of a deleted tenant is presented to Firestore, with a surviving sibling tenant as control.

observation.method: Accounts with one localId in two tenants (and the project) read documents whose rules need both the uid and firebase.tenant, through get, batchGet and runQuery; then tenant A is deleted and A's unexpired token is sent on get, runQuery and a create, with tenant B's token as control. Tenants are created and deleted as fixture setup.

localEvidence.limits: Local strict-profile tests refuse a deleted tenant's token (the tenant store is gone, so the token's tenant no longer matches); the default emulator profile admits the same unsigned token as a mock token. Production is unobserved.

conditions.note: A read-only transaction opened with one principal's token is used with another principal's, another tenant's and no credential. End users cannot open read-write transactions (FS-RULES/document-access), so this is the only server-side transaction an end user holds.

observation.method: Principal A opens a read-only transaction (BeginTransaction readOnly, and newTransaction.readOnly on runQuery and batchGet); the transaction ID is then used with B's token, a tenant principal's token and no credential for batchGet and runQuery on documents only A may read: whether the ID is bound to its principal and under which principal Rules evaluate.

conditions.note: A validly signed ID token issued by another Firebase project's Auth is presented to Firestore on the sandbox, with a same-project control.

observation.method: One @example.com test user created on fireemu-oracle-query (X9), its ID token taken and the user deleted and read back at once; the token is sent on get and runQuery of an open and an owner-only document on fireemu-oracle-idp, over REST and gRPC, beside the same requests with an idp token.

conditions.note: A Web SDK runTransaction (batchGet reads, then one Commit with preconditions and verify writes) across a sign-out or a principal switch between its reads and its commit.

observation.method: Node Web SDK runTransaction on Rules-protected documents with a sign-out, and separately an A-to-B switch, after the reads and before the commit; record the principal and outcome of the Commit, the number of update-function calls and the server post-state, with an unchanged-principal control.

conditions.note: Active document and query listeners under Rules through sign-out (catalog case 106, moved here from FS-LISTEN-SDK by R2) and through a switch from principal A to B.

observation.method: Pinned Web SDK document and query listeners on Rules-protected data; sign out, and separately switch A to B, then commit changes the new principal may and may not read; record server snapshots, errors and listener ends against a static-principal witness.

localEvidence.limits: The local scenario AUTH-FS-CROSS.auth-switch-rules-listen is unobserved in production.

conditions.note: Active document and query listeners across a claim change with a forced token refresh, and a native listen stream held past its token's expiry allowance.

observation.method: Node Web SDK listeners on documents whose rules need claim c: add c then getIdToken(true), remove c then getIdToken(true), each probed by a commit; a native gRPC Listen opened with a token and held past exp + 30 s (FS-RULES/token-expiry) without refresh, probed by commits before and after.

conditions.note: Active document and query listeners after the principal's refresh tokens are revoked (catalog cases 109 and 109C, moved here from FS-LISTEN-SDK by R2), the account is disabled, or the account is deleted.

observation.method: Node Web SDK and native gRPC listeners probed by commits right after the change and around the token's expiry, within one window long enough to pass exp + 30 s (OX-3); a quiet window never counts as evidence of absence. FS-RULES/token-states observed that unary requests keep accepting such tokens until expiry.

conditions.note: Active document and query listeners of a tenant principal when the tenant is deleted, with a same-UID principal of a surviving tenant as control.

observation.method: Native gRPC and Node Web SDK listeners opened before the deletion, probed by commits after it; record REMOVE, errors, stream ends and snapshots on both tenants.

localEvidence.limits: Local in-process listener tests end the deleted tenant's target (REMOVE cause 16, then UNAUTHENTICATED and EOF) under the strict profile; the default emulator profile does not. Production is unobserved.

conditions.note: A Web SDK write left pending by one principal when the user switches to another or signs out: what the backend receives and does.

observation.method: With the network disabled, A writes; switch to B (and separately sign out), enable the network, then switch back to A; record whether and with which token the write is sent, its outcome and the server state at each step. Display differences inside the SDK are out of scope (FS-LISTEN-SDK OL-2).

conditions.note: The final artifact's AUTH-FS-CROSS comparison, with the FS-RULES comparison re-run on the same artifact because the unary conditions moved there.

observation.method: Replay every AUTH-FS-CROSS recipe and the FS-RULES corpus on one final source-bound artifact.

conditions.note: Independent clean-context closure review and a separate safety review of every change that widens what a request may do.

observation.method: Independent review of scope, conditions, receipts, divergences, cleanup and owner decisions.
